text: Social judgment theory involves how people process information, form attitudes, and respond to differing opinions. Sherif & Hovland [ 38 ] proposed social judgment theory in 1961, asserting that everyone holds a basic stance on a particular issue, referred to as the “anchor point. “The anchor point reflects an individual’s core attitude or opinion on an issue, serving as the benchmark for judging other opinions.
